chunks.arabic_text: ٢٧ - عَلِيّ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الْخَدِيجِيّ

translations.en: 27 - Ali ibn Abdullah, Abu al-Hasan al-Khadiji

chunks.arabic_text: لِأَنَّهُ يُنْسَبُ إِلَى وَلَدِ أَبِي هَالَةَ، النَّبَّاشِ، الْأَسَدِيّ، الَّذِي كَانَ زَوْجَ خَدِيجَةَ (عَلَيْهَا السَّلَام) قَبْلَ النَّبِيِّ (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَسَلَّم) - لَهُ مَقَالَةٌ. لَا يُلْتَفَتُ إِلَيْهِ، وَلَا يُرْتَفَعُ بِهِ.

translations.en: because he is ascribed to the child of Abu Hala, al-Nabbash al-Asadi, who was the husband of Khadija (peace be upon her) before the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) - he has a doctrine. He is not turned to, and one does not ascend by him.

en.summary: This entry from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Ghada'iri’s *Kitab al-Du'afa* identifies Ali ibn Abdullah as a relatively obscure narrator whose nisba 'al-Khadiji' links him genealogically to al-Nabbash al-Asadi, the pre-Islamic husband of Khadija bint Khuwaylid. Al-Ghada'iri classifies him as *la yultafat ilayhi* (not relied upon) and *la yarfa'u bihi* (does not elevate), indicating his hadith are neither strong enough to stand alone nor sufficient to corroborate stronger narrators, reflecting the critical scrutiny applied to lesser-known figures in Shia biographical evaluation.
en.seo_question: Who is Ali ibn Abdullah al-Khadiji and why is he considered weak in hadith sciences?

key_terms.الْخَدِيجِيّ: Al-Khadiji: A nisba (attributive name) indicating lineage or association with Khadija.
key_terms.النَّبَّاش: Al-Nabbash: A specific name or epithet of the ancestor mentioned.
key_terms.مَقَالَةٌ: Maqalah: A doctrine, opinion, or distinct view held by the narrator.
key_terms.لَا يُلْتَفَتُ إِلَيْهِ: La yul'tafu ilayhi: He is not turned to; his narration is not relied upon due to weakness.
key_terms.وَلَا يُرْتَفَعُ بِهِ: Wa la yurtafa'u bihi: One does not ascend by him; his narration is not used to elevate the grade of a hadith.
